messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple nodes in us-west2-gpu-pool reporting repeated container restarts and CUDA OOMs. auto-escalation threshold reached. possible memory creep in KV cache / paged-attention allocator. affected: ~6 nodes, partial customer 503s. tagging as P1. thread created 2468009999

alex: seeing the same on dashboards — token latencies spike then node flaps. traces show heavy paging activity before OOM. samples from node-42: `OOM when allocating 3.2GiB` then container restart.

priya: stack traces look like allocator fragmentation not immediate leak — slow DRIFT. eviction not keeping up. I pulled kv alloc histograms: free-slab segments steadily decreasing over 8h.

sam: quick logs from node-42 (last 3 mins):
```
[2026-06-12T02:12:37Z] runtime: warn: attention_pager: page_in_latency=289ms pages=121
[2026-06-12T02:12:38Z] cuda: ERROR cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory at kernel launch
[2026-06-12T02:12:39Z] allocator: slab_fragmentation > 0.78, free_slots=120 -> 63
[2026-06-12T02:12:40Z] process: restart triggered (exit code 137)
```

taylor: confirmed nvidia-smi snapshot shows GPU memory at 95% then spikes to 100% right before OOM. looks like KV warmup for certain tenants holding slots.

jordan: initial impact assessment: ~12 customers saw 5xxs in last 40m, but only 3 had sustained errors (20-30% of requests). no data exfiltration. CS: prepare messaging if we need to extend ETA.

alex: mitigation options: (1) aggressive eviction flip for KV cache on affected nodes, (2) temporarily disable attention paging (force non-paged allocator) for model-family=redwood-llama-1 on these nodes, (3) reduce concurrency on node pool, (4) cordon & drain hot nodes to evict state and restart clean.

priya: prefer (1) + (4) immediate. (2) is heavier but safe as fallback — it'll increase token cost/latency but avoids OOM.

sam: executing eviction toggle now on us-west2-gpu-pool: `redwoodctl runtime config set --pool us-west2-gpu-pool kv.eviction.aggressiveness=high --ttl 15m`

eng-sre-bot: COMMAND OK: set kv.eviction.aggressiveness=high on pool us-west2-gpu-pool (request id r-9f3b).

sam: also starting gradual cordon & drain of 3 hottest nodes (node-42, node-43, node-47) one at a time. running: `redwoodctl node drain node-42 --grace-period 60s`

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic fallback policy will route requests to dedicated-fallback-tier for affected customers when node capacity < 40%.

alex: while drain runs, let's monitor slab metrics and per-tenant KV usage. priya, can you check whether any tenant has disproportionate slot retention (i.e., not releasing KV slots after short-LIFO)?

priya: on it. quick query: `select tenant_id, avg(kv_slot_hold_seconds) from kv_metrics where pool='us-west2-gpu-pool' and time>now()-6h group by tenant_id order by avg desc limit 10` -> top tenant t-132 has avg 15m hold, expected 30s-90s. looks like warmup behavior + a small leak in their workload. I'll open per-tenant note.

jordan: CS: I'm drafting a short notification for impacted customers: brief, what happened, mitigation in flight, ETA for full restoration ~30-60m. Will wait for alex/priya ack.

sam: node-42 drain complete, restarted runtime. post-restart free_slots jumped from 63 -> 420. memory stable for 5m post-restart. moving to node-43 now.

alex: good. still seeing paging on node-43 but eviction seems to be lowering pressure. keep drains sequential.

priya: temporary policy to cap per-tenant KV slots to 256 in this pool applied: `redwoodctl runtime policy apply --pool us-west2-gpu-pool limit.kv_slots.per_tenant=256 --ttl 30m` — this should blunt the biggest offenders while we investigate further.

eng-sre-bot: COMMAND OK: applied per-tenant kv slot cap (request id r-a72c).

taylor: quick note on rollback risk: if we disable paging (non-paged mode) CPU and token latency will increase ~20-40% for long-context requests. be ready to revert if latency impact unacceptable for premium customers.

jordan: CS update sent to impacted customers (internal draft): "We're investigating increased errors affecting generation API in us-west2 due to memory fragmentation on GPU nodes. Mitigations are being applied, and we expect service to be restored for most customers within 60 minutes. We'll follow up with root-cause once complete."

alex: monitoring window now. if drains + eviction don't stabilize in 20m, we'll escalate to temporary paging disable on pool. Sam, keep running `nvtop`/`nvidia-smi` sampling and post spikes.

sam: copying nvtop logs to thread:
```
node-43 @ 02:34:21 - gpu0 mem 12.3Gi/16Gi (76%)
node-43 @ 02:35:03 - gpu0 mem 15.8Gi/16Gi (98%) -> spike correlated with tenant t-132 requests
node-43 @ 02:36:10 - container restart (exit 137)
```

priya: I'm attaching quick repro trace for devs: gist link https://gist.redwood/repro/kv-drift-2468 (contains sample trace and heap snapshot). early diff indicates allocator metadata fragmentation: many small free segments scattered across slabs preventing coalescing during runtime.

alex: next steps for postmortem: 1) root-cause: why fragmentation grows without reclaim, 2) whether eviction policy has blind spots for warmup workloads, 3) whether compacting GC or slab defrag routine can be made opportunistic during low load, 4) add per-tenant KV slot alerts.

jordan: CS: adding note to customers impacted that we may need to schedule a maintenance window for a longer fix if the root cause requires allocator patching. will coordinate timing after eng postmortem.

eng-sre-bot: ALERT: new restart on node-47 at 2468010305. currently cordoning node-47 manually to avoid cascading.

sam: cordon complete for node-47. draining now.

alex: handing off to night oncall: priya will continue watch and follow up on per-tenant traces. I'm off in 15m. Priya, please escalate to runtime-team if you see >2 more restarts.

priya: acknowledged. will continue monitoring and loop in runtime and allocator owners. filing incident ticket INC-2468009999 with summary and actions taken.

cs-ops: thank you all — I updated the customer-facing status page with the latest note. will send follow-up after full recovery.

incident-bot: HANDOFF: incident P1 handed to oncall priya (next shift). incident created 2468009999, last update 2468010360.

alex: thanks team. postmortem owners: priya (investigation & allocator fix), sam (runtime ops), taylor (performance impact & benchmarks), jordan (customer comms).

priya: starting RCA doc skeleton now and will attach profiler dumps.

sam: will produce timeline + node-level histograms and link into RCA.

jordan: leaving a note to schedule follow-up review with CS and product later this week.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigations applied (eviction aggressiveness=high, per-tenant cap=256, 3 nodes drained). monitoring continues."
